ops.oldText: (f) actual or alleged infringement of any Third Party's Intellectual Property by the Product or by either Party in performing its duties or obligations hereunder with respect to the Product

quote: SFJ shall be the sole and exclusive owner of the Trial Data Package including the Research Results included therein.
rationale: We retain ownership of all Existing PB Intellectual Property and Trial Inventions and buy back the Trial Data Package on the earlier of approval or termination, so ownership ends with us; however SFJ takes a first-priority security interest over all of our IP (7.1), can force a Program Transfer of the whole programme on specified defaults (3.20), and can gate our out-licensing (7.5.5). proposal.comment: [Playbook] Our position is a mutual aggregate cap with uncapped carve-outs for indemnities, confidentiality/data protection, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and IP infringement. We have kept our Article 6 and Section 14.2 payment obligations outside the cap so the economics are unaffected.

ops.newText: FOR THE AVOIDANCE OF DOUBT, THIS SECTION 15.11 IS NOT MEANT TO LIMIT PB'S OBLIGATION TO PAY SFJ THE AMOUNTS SET FORTH IN ARTICLE 6 OR SECTION 14.2. EXCEPT FOR EXCLUDED CLAIMS AND PB'S PAYMENT OBLIGATIONS UNDER ARTICLE 6 AND SECTION 14.2, EACH PARTY'S TOTAL AGGREGATE LIABILITY FOR DAMAGES ARISING OUT OF OR RELATING TO THIS AGREEMENT SHALL NOT EXCEED THE GREATER OF (A) THE DEVELOPMENT COSTS ACTUALLY PAID OR INCURRED BY SFJ HEREUNDER AND (B) ONE MILLION U.S. DOLLARS ($1,000,000). "EXCLUDED CLAIMS" MEANS A PARTY'S BREACH OF ITS CONFIDENTIALITY OR DATA PROTECTION OBLIGATIONS, ITS INDEMNIFICATION OBLIGATIONS, ITS GROSS NEGLIGENCE, WILFUL MISCONDUCT OR FRAUD, AND ITS INFRINGEMENT OF THE OTHER PARTY'S INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY RIGHTS.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] A vendor termination or re-pricing right triggered by our change of control is not acceptable; assumption of obligations by the successor protects SFJ's economics.

ops.newText: SFJ shall have no right to terminate this Agreement, and no additional payment shall become due from PB, solely by reason of a Change of Control of PB, provided that the successor assumes PB's obligations under this Agreement.
ops.oldText: SFJ may, in its sole discretion, terminate this Agreement in its entirety at any time following a Change of Control of PB that occurs prior to the date of payment by PB of the final Approval Payment.

proposal.summary: Section 15.6 sensibly permits assignment to affiliates and successors, but Section 14.2.6 lets SFJ terminate on our change of control and charge 150% of Development Costs, which is walk-away territory for us. We have removed the change-of-control termination right where the successor assumes our obligations.

rationale: The only exclusivity runs against SFJ and in our favour, so there is nothing to redline under this rule.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We do not accept liquidated damages against us; because we also remain liable for Approval Payments, a repayment of SFJ's actual funding is the appropriate exit amount. The 150% and 25%-interest formulas elsewhere in Section 14.2 should be conformed.

ops.newText: PB will pay SFJ, within ninety (90) days of the date of termination, an amount equal to one hundred percent (100%) of Development Costs paid or incurred by SFJ prior to such termination.
ops.oldText: PB will pay SFJ, within [***] of the date of termination, an amount equal to three hundred percent (300%) of Development Costs paid or incurred by SFJ prior to such termination.

proposal.summary: Termination triggers fixed multiples payable by us — 300% of Development Costs (14.2.1, 14.2.2, 14.2.5.2, 14.2.7), 150% on a change of control or compliance breach, and Development Costs plus 25% interest under 14.2.10 — all on top of continuing Approval Payments; these are liquidated damages far beyond our 3-months'-fees fallback. We have reduced the convenience-termination multiple to a return of funding.

quote: All rights not exclusively granted to SFJ are reserved to PB and its Affiliates.
rationale: No licence is granted to us because we retain ownership of the Product IP, so the licence-scope rule is not engaged.

quote: PB shall not, without SFJ's prior written consent, enter into a Licensing Transaction unless such Licensing Transaction is an Excluded Licensing Transaction
rationale: No field-of-use or non-compete restriction binds us; the only competitive restraint (Section 3.19) binds SFJ. We note the Section 7.5.5 consent gate on Licensing Transactions as a financing covenant (mitigated by the Excluded Licensing Transaction carve-outs and expedited arbitration), which we have raised under the IP/security package review.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We need an unconditional right to terminate for convenience on notice (30 days preferred, 60 days as fallback), not one gated on a funding threshold and the pre-approval window.

ops.newText: PB may terminate this Agreement at any time upon sixty (60) days' prior written notice to SFJ.
ops.oldText: PB may terminate this Agreement at any time after SFJ has paid or incurred a total of $60 million of Development Costs and prior to the date of receipt of the first Regulatory Approval upon [***] prior written notice to SFJ.

proposal.summary: Our only convenience right is gated on SFJ having funded $60M and on the pre-approval period, while SFJ has several unilateral exit rights (Material Adverse Event, change of control, JSC disagreement); our playbook requires an unconditional Customer exit on notice. We have removed the gating conditions and set a 60-day notice period.

quote: PB shall (a) provide SFJ with quarterly unaudited financial statements and annual audited financial statements
rationale: There is no usage-verification or audit right allowing SFJ into our systems; the information rights are periodic financial reporting and mutual quality-audit reports, which we accept.

quote: will be governed by the internal laws of the State of Delaware, USA
rationale: Delaware law sits at our accepted fallback and the arbitration is seated in New York under ICDR rules, so no foreign seat; we note only that we would prefer courts to mandatory arbitration.
We found no most-favoured-nation, best-terms or price-matching obligation binding us anywhere in the Agreement.

quote: PB shall spend at least an amount equal to the amount of funding paid by SFJ to PB pursuant to this Section 4.2.
rationale: There is no take-or-pay or volume commitment; we control the Elected Total Amount ($110–120M) and the spend covenant simply requires funding to be applied to the programme.
ruleTitle: Minimum purchase commitments and volume restrictions on Customer

quote: During the Term and for a period of [***] thereafter, neither Party shall solicit an employee of the other Party who is or has been involved in the performance or oversight of any of the development activities hereunder
rationale: The non-solicit is mutual, limited to personnel involved in the programme, contains a general-advertising carve-out and includes no no-hire, which meets our fallback; we should confirm the redacted tail period is no more than 12 months.

quote: The term of this Agreement (the "Term") will commence on the Effective Date and will expire upon the earliest of (i) termination of this Agreement in accordance with Section 14.2
rationale: The Term runs to the final Approval Payment with no automatic renewal, notice window or price-uplift mechanic, so there is nothing to shorten or cap.

quote: effective as of such termination, SFJ shall, and it hereby does, assign to PB all of SFJ's and its Affiliates' right, title and interest in and to all Product Filings then owned or Controlled by SFJ or any of its Affiliates
rationale: Section 14.3 gives us assignment of the Trial Data Package and Product Filings, delivery of all data, transfer or wind-down of ongoing trials and assignment of CRO/site agreements — better than our preferred exit package.
